svg.title: Decision 0547 question 4: End facing with a Part extent on stock taller than the requested area, and options A, B and C
svg.text: Question 4: the first band of a slice when the stock is 3.0 mm taller than the requested area (Stepdown 1.3 mm)
Looking along X at the end face. Up the page is up the tool. 20 px = 1 mm in height; the tool's flutes reach well above the band.

g.text: Today, and option C
requested area
mm
The first band's tip is 1.3 mm below the area's
top, but its flutes also take the 3.0 mm of stock
above it: 4.3 mm deep, 3.3 times the Stepdown.
Option C keeps this cut and does not flag it
(the check ignores the stock above the area).
Option A (the owner's answer)
Three passes are added from the stock's top
down to the area: 1.3, 1.3 and 0.4 mm, across
the area's width only. Then the area's own bands,
1.3 mm each. Same material removed as today.
About 6 s more per slice in this example (20 mm
wide area, 1 mm slice and approach, F1000, plunge
300: each added pass about 2 s). A note says so.
Option B
No path. The message says the band
cuts 4.3 mm deep along the tool, more
than the Stepdown of 1.3 mm: lower the
Stepdown, or face the stock above first.
The user must face the stock down
first (a Whole stock End facing, say)
before a Part extent End facing runs.

svg.text: Why Whole stock is unaffected, and why this is the usual case for a Part extent
With Whole stock the requested area is the stock's own outline, so its top is the stock's top: there is no stock above it.
A Part extent asks to face only the part's outline; the stock is almost always larger than the part, so it rises above it.
The extra depth comes from the flutes being longer than a band, not from A turning: End facing keeps A fixed while cutting.
Generated G-code remains the user's to verify before it is run on a machine.
